'''The Workstation Task Post Mortem''' records why the omnidev task
<code>task_omnidev_workstation_new_board_channel</code> consumed roughly 16 hours
and roughly 400 million prompt tokens over 29 executor threads and
'''never completed'''.

== Verdict ==

The premise that the harness is basically the same cordis runtime as the
workbench, so it should just work, is '''half true - and the false half is not
the expensive half'''. The facility itself - a Node image, a run-time cordis
config, a profile-gated compose service and the board, channel, workflow and
templates - was genuinely a mirror of the workbench and was built, pushed and
even published to the container registry inside the first four executions.

What consumed roughly 11 of the 16 hours was '''one acceptance criterion the
operator never asked for in the clarified process''': proof that the harness boots
with the plugin set and reaches email, sms, totp and browser. That criterion was
(a) not part of mirroring the workbench deployment, (b) genuinely harder than the
rest, because the plugins were not drop-in for the harness (different tool-call
payload key and different credentials file format), and (c) partially
contradictory with the cost rule that external services must not live in the
workstation image.

|what=cost and root causes of an over-specified workstation task
|where=the omnidev board, task ..._workstation_new_board_channel
|status=never completed, task left in backlog
|source=Projects/Omniagent/Workstation-Task-Post-Mortem.md

== Measured cost ==

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Metric !! Value
|-
| Task-attached executor threads || 29
|-
| LLM calls || 3 864
|-
| Prompt tokens || 400 494 967
|-
| Completion tokens || 16 741 219
|-
| Cached prompt tokens || 353 669 248 (88.3 percent cache hit)
|-
| Wall clock, first thread start to last thread end || 15 h 52 m
|-
| Largest single-call prompt context || 17 943 219 tokens
|-
| Compaction prompt messages || 3 169
|}

Eight consecutive executions stopped at exactly 297 to 300 of 300 LLM calls. A
retry creates a new thread that re-reads the repository from scratch, at roughly
35 million prompt tokens per thread; in total the range recorded 3 291 file reads
and 1 612 greps against 80 edit operations. At an average of roughly 103 600
prompt tokens per call, the redundant read and verify pattern is what paid the
bill.

== Root causes, ranked ==

# '''Over-specified acceptance criterion inside one task''' - the dominant cause.
   The capability proof was not in the operator's clarified process and generated
   the reject and rework cycles that followed.
# '''Per-execution budget with no carry-over''' - serial amnesia. Nothing forced a
   smaller, verifiable unit of work, and the only exit was a human-gated thread
   failure.
# '''Context churn''' - thousands of compaction prompts and repeated reads.
# '''Provider balance exhausted''' - the tail of the window ended in payment
   errors, and the dispatcher re-entered the next workflow step with a fresh
   thread each time, so the last eleven review threads died on their first
   provider call with zero LLM calls.

== Lessons carried into the standard config ==

* Split a large facility from its capability proof: land the mirror, then verify
  capabilities in their own task with their own budget.
* Keep the acceptance criteria to what the operator actually asked for; an
  unrequested proof is where an unbounded read and verify loop starts.
* Make a retry able to resume rather than re-derive, so a fresh thread does not
  re-read the whole tree.

These lessons sit alongside the deliberate decisions recorded in
[[Workstation Standard Config]], the native plugin layout in
[[Workstation Compat Layer]], and the executor-versus-tester boundary and tool
priority in [[Plugin Tool Awareness]].
